ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Place object A with mass $m_{\mathrm{A}} = 100\mathrm{g}$ on top of a spring and connect it to the spring. The lower end of the spring is connected to object B with mass $m_{\mathrm{B}} = 200\mathrm{g}$, which is placed on the ground, forming a vertical spring oscillator that allows A to vibrate up and down. The natural length of the spring is $10\mathrm{cm}$, and the spring constant is $k = 50\mathrm{N/m}$. The thicknesses of A and B are negligible, and $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. When the system undergoes simple harmonic motion, find the height of the equilibrium position of A from the ground.
2. If spring does not stretch during the vibration of object A, find the maximum pressure exerted by object B on the ground when object A vibrates with the maximum amplitude.
3. Based on question (2), how much work is done by the spring force on object A from the equilibrium position to the lowest point?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, block A is located above, and a vertical spring is connected between A and the lower block B; block B is placed on the horizontal ground marked with diagonal lines. Both figures represent the same structure: A is at the upper end of the spring, and B is at the lower end of the spring and in contact with the ground. Then reason: Let the spring compression be x, the spring's natural length L0=10 cm=0.10 m, and x>0 when compressed. Since the thicknesses of A and B are ignored, the height of A above the ground equals the instantaneous length of the spring. 1. When A is at the equilibrium position, the spring force is upward and gravity is downward, so kx0=mA g. mA=0.100 kg, so x0=(0.100×10)/50=0.020 m=2 cm. At equilibrium, the spring length is L0-x0=10 cm-2 cm=8 cm, so the height of A's equilibrium position is 8 cm. 2. To make A vibrate with the maximum amplitude and the spring never stretch, the highest point is just the natural length of the spring, that is, x=0. The equilibrium compression is x0=2 cm, so the amplitude is 2 cm; the compression at the lowest point is x=2x0=4 cm=0.040 m. At this time, the downward force of the spring on B is maximum, equal to kx=50×0.040=2 N. The gravity of B is mB g=0.200×10=2 N, so the maximum supporting force of the ground on B, that is, the maximum pressure of B on the ground, is 2+2=4 N. 3. From the equilibrium position to the lowest point, x increases from 0.020 m to 0.040 m, and A moves downward, while the elastic force of the compressed spring on A is upward, so the signed work done by the spring force on A is negative: W_s=-∫_{0.020}^{0.040} kx dx=-0.5×50×(0.040^2-0.020^2)=-0.03 J. If the problem only asks for the numerical magnitude of "how much work is done," then the magnitude of the work done by the spring force is 0.03 J.
